global.text: Just counted my strongbox twice. {gold} gold and not a single coin cost me a sword swing. Business is beautiful.
My caravan guards number {troop_count} now. Bandits can keep their pride, I'll keep the profit, thanks.
Took {fief} last month with {troop_count} men and a very fair offer. Mostly fair. Nobody bled, everybody paid.
Lost two wagons to bandits this week, yet I'm still up {gold} gold. Call it a win, I'm not complaining.
My guards outnumber the tax collectors in {fief} now. Healthiest market I've seen in years, truly.
Everyone wants to talk battles. I'd rather talk about the {gold} gold I made while they were busy fighting.
{troop_count} sellswords on my payroll and not one has asked for a pension yet. Miracles happen, ser.
Winning is exhausting. Thank the gods for ledgers, they never ask how the war went, only what it cost.
Anyone thinking of raiding my road should check the price of {troop_count} spears first. Ask me how I know.
Pay the hired blades, sell the surplus wool, and {fief} still owes me a drink for the escort. Good week.
Rain again over the {town} road. Mud means slower carts and fatter costs, so my mood is about as damp as my boots.
Whoever keeps moving the map markers, please stop. I lost a whole morning to a route that isn't there anymore.
Lag spike just ate my caravan halfway to {village}. Two crates of spice and a very confused mule.
If the toll gate at {village} wants one more copper per cart, I'm building a bridge out of spite.
Someone tell me why a sack of barley costs more than a horse in {town} now. I'd like a word with whoever set that.
Quiet morning on the trade roads. I don't trust it. Quiet roads usually mean someone's lurking in the hedges.
A merchant, a mule and a map walk into an inn. Only two of them could read the price board.
Sold out of salt in {town} before noon. Some of you should set your alarms earlier.
Honest question: does anyone actually enjoy the long haul through the hills, or do we all just tolerate it for the profit?
Sunset over the river was lovely. Shame it cost me a day's wages in tolls to get there.
Three caravans hit by bandits on the north road this week. Insurance is not a real thing here, apparently.
Tolls at the {town} bridge went up again. Nobody asked the people actually paying them, mind.
{rival} undercut my spice prices by half. Either they found a secret supply or they're just losing money on purpose.
Whoever balanced iron ore spawns, I'd like a word. Mining three days for one ingot is not a trade route.
Bandits on the coast road again. I'd pay a guard fee gladly if anyone sold one that actually shows up.
Lost a whole wagon of salt to the swamp path ambush. Lovely. Next time I bring the tax collector along for company.
Grain prices in {town} are a joke. Someone is cornering the market and I'd love to know who.
The new toll on the river crossing means every cart loses a third of its profit before it even moves. Dreadful.
Honest question for the devs: why does a sack of flour weigh more than a horse? My back disagrees with the balance.
{faction} wants the mountain pass closed for their war. Wonderful. My cloth is sitting in a warehouse rotting.
Our caravan guards for {fief} are paid well, and the road bonus comes on top of the wage. Ask within.
Need hands for a siege of {fief}? I'll cover rations and a share of the spoils. Who's in?
Anyone fancy a raid on the {enemy_faction} wagon train? Split the take fifty-fifty, no questions asked.
My ledger says {enemy_faction} tolls have ruined the road to {fief}. Time to fix that, with swords.
{enemy_faction} thinks their walls will keep us out of {fief}. Their toll clerks will fold first, mark my words.
Hauling supplies to the siege camp at {fief} takes more backs than I have. Come earn some coin.
Honest question: would any of you join {my_faction} for a campaign? Pay is on time, I promise, mostly.
A good raid is a bad investment unless the escort list is full. Sign on with {my_faction} before we leave.
Forty crowns in advance for anyone who can hold a pike at {fief} by dawn. Hell of a deal, and I mean it.
Every war needs quartermasters, not just knights. If you can count sacks, {my_faction} needs you.
Bolts of dyed wool moving fast in {town}. Good prices for anyone with a cart and a bit of nerve.
Who here is buying grain in {town}? I will sell you a sack at a fair price, no haggling games.
Saw iron ingots going for {gold} in {town} today. Someone is hoarding and I want to know who.
Ser, a caravan of salt leaves {town} at dawn. Hire a guard or pay the toll, your choice.
Honest question: is anyone still paying {gold} for a good mule? Prices have gone mad lately.
Every time the road to {town} closes, my margins bleed out. Somebody please clear the bandits already.
Trading tip: buy hides when the autumn caravans are in and sell them back in winter. Works every year.
Looking to swap spice for timber. Fair rate, no tricks, and I will even throw in a barrel of ale.
The toll at the bridge went up again. I am not complaining, I am just writing my accounts in ink so I remember it.
Anyone needing a cart repaired in {town}? I will trade the work for a few sacks of oats, fair deal.
Lost a field fight to {player} and the wagon train took the hit. Somebody owes me a refund on that escort.
Fine, {player} won the field. Now every road trader in Ormerath will pay for it in tolls. Thanks a lot.
Five hundred gold in mercenary pay, gone in one afternoon. Remind me never to hire swords near {player}.
Another battle lost, another ledger in the red. Whoever keeps picking fights with {player} is bad for trade.
Ran the numbers on today's fight. Losses outweigh the loot by a mile. Expect higher prices from my stalls.
Our line broke at the ford. Good for {player}, terrible for anyone trying to ship grain through there.
Lost {troop_count} men and the cart with them. Next time I'm paying for insurance I actually read.
The fight is over, the bill is not. Those {troop_count} hired blades cost more than they earned me.
Congratulations to {player}, I suppose. Every victory like that scares off the caravans I need.
Win or lose, the road tax still comes due. Today it came due twice. Hope the spoils were worth it.

whisper.text: Enjoy the field, {player}. I'll be remembering the price of those {troop_count} crossbows for a long while.
Well fought, I'll admit. Doesn't change that you cost me a shipment of salt. We'll be square eventually.
A win is a win, but you've made my routes twice as dangerous. My next insurance premium is on you.
Keep your victory. I'll be sending my prices up on every wagon heading toward your holdings. Consider it a tax.
I'm not sore about losing the field. I'm sore that you took it on a road I use. Find another one.
That was expensive, {player}. The mercenaries want paying and the buyers want their goods. Neither cares who won.
Lost {troop_count} men today. I'm not after blood, just a fair accounting. Consider the bill sent.
You beat me fair, and I respect a good position. But my caravans won't be crossing your land again.
Don't pretend you did this for peace. You did it for the spoils. I'll find my margin somewhere else.
Next time you want to fight, let's talk terms first. Losing a battle is a lot cheaper than losing a route.

face.text: {player}. Good work on the field, I'll give you that. Now I'm three wagons short and in a foul mood, so mind your step.
You caught my line on the ridge and turned it inside out. Clever, if you ask a merchant. Expensive, if you ask my accountant.
Save the victory speech. I have {troop_count} men to pay and a cargo that won't be selling anywhere near as well now.
Lost the field, lost the wagons, lost my patience. Don't expect me to smile at you until I've rebuilt the ledger.
Fine, you won. I'll be counting every coin I owe to get back on my feet, and I'll remember who made that necessary.
Stand aside, {player}. My men are carting the wounded and my pride is somewhere in the mud back there.
Every battle you win is a tariff on my trade routes, you know. The crown won't pay my losses for me.
The field's yours, but the road beyond it still belongs to me. Tolls, insurance, and a sour attitude. You're welcome.
I'd offer you a drink, but I'm busy calculating what a stolen cart is worth. Hope the loot covers the mood.
You broke my formation and my week in one afternoon. I'll survive. Just don't expect me to wave on the way past.

global.text: Battle at the ford ended with {player} on top. Prices on the east road will likely wobble for a few days.
Field fight outcome noted. Losses on my side are manageable. Caravans resume tomorrow at the usual rate.
Lost a skirmish, not a season. Trade lanes don't close over one bad afternoon, whatever the rumors say.
Wagon losses this morning are going on my ledger. If anyone needs freight hauled, I'm still taking orders.
Hard day in the field. Still, a broken line makes for a cheaper road than a broken market, so I'll take it.
Anyone else seeing grain prices spike after the skirmish? Could be the rumors, could be the {troop_count} carts missing.
Field results are in. Nobody's happy, nobody's ruined. Back to haggling over fodder at the usual stalls.
Some traders gamble on war. I just count the cost afterward. Today's count is not encouraging, but it's survivable.
The contract on the river crossing is off until the dust settles. Anyone with a claim, send it in writing.
Lost the field to {player}. Fair enough, the terrain favored them. Will be looking at better scouting next time.

whisper.text: Good fight, {player}. My men are regrouping and my ledger is bleeding, but the books will balance eventually.
I suspect you know the cost of that battle already. If you'd like to talk trade rather than swords, I'm listening.
Lost the field this morning. Not the end of my world, just the end of a good week. Care to make it up in trade?
The road through your valley is still open to me, I assume? I'd rather not renegotiate my tolls after today.
Battles come and go. My wagons come and go. I'd like to keep my wagons intact, so let's keep this civil.
You outmaneuvered us cleanly. I'll write that down as a lesson in terrain, not a grudge. Ledger's clean on my side.
I've got {troop_count} men limping back to camp. Could you tell me which roads your people will be patrolling?
No hard feelings, {player}. Just let me know before your next skirmish, so I can route the convoys around it.
We lost the field, you kept it. I'd rather hear your terms than keep guessing. Shall we talk over a cup?
Hope your men are paid well for this. Mine will be paid late, which is a lesson I should have learned sooner.

face.text: {player}. That was a tidy win on the ridge. Mind if I ask where your supply line runs? It might be worth knowing.
Lost the field, not the argument about prices. I'll be by your camp tomorrow, if you're interested in some salt.
Good ground choice, I'll admit. My scouts missed the marsh. Lesson learned, and I'm not sore about it, really.
Your men fought well. Mine fought well enough. The difference was the mud, and I'll be sure to look at maps next time.
Field's yours. The wagons are mine, and I'd like to get them moving before the rain. Could you point me to an open road?
Morning, {player}. No need for swords today. I'm more interested in whether this battle changes the price of oats.
We lost. Accept it and move on. Two hundred gold worth of mercenaries makes a poor argument in a court of law.
Hmm. You won and I'm short on cash. Doesn't mean I can't be civil. Mind if I buy you a meal at the inn?
The fight's over, and I've got a cart to repair. If you need anything hauled, I'm still in the business.
Let's call it even on pride, since the field went your way. There's still plenty of coin to be made here.

global.text: Lost the field, but {player} fought square and didn't burn the carts. Honest win, honest loss. Respect.
Congrats to {player} on the ridge. Drinks at the inn on me, once my wagons stop smelling of smoke.
Battle went to {player} today. Good thing I fund half their supply lines. Who says we can't both profit?
Lost a few wagons at the ford. Whoever set that trap, I'd like to buy them a round after I've counted the damage.
The field went to {player}, and I'm honestly glad someone sensible is holding the high road. Keep it open for traders.
Good battle, all things considered. Bloodied but in business. See you at the next caravan run, {player}.
Took a beating in the field, but my accountants say we're fine. Strong contracts carry you through bad afternoons.
Lost the ridge fight to {player}. Next week's supply run is still on, and I'll be bringing extra bolts of wool.
Honest fight, honest losses. I'd take a loss to a friend over a win to a bandit any day. Keep the roads clear, {player}.
Our lines broke at the ford. Good news is {player} doesn't hold grudges, so the next trade deal is already sketched.

whisper.text: Don't let the field get you down, {player}. The ridge was a rough spot, and I'd still trust you with my cargo.
I heard the battle went your way. Drop a line when you have a moment, I've got a profitable proposal in mind.
Lost a few carts, but you kept your word and that matters more to me. Want to renegotiate our next shipment together?
Your men held their ground well today. My men ran. I'll pay you the difference next time we share a table.
No hard feelings from my side, truly. Let's talk about a future convoy before the bandits notice we're both wounded.
Was the fight worth it for you, {player}? I'd much rather you saved those swords for the highway robbers.
The damage isn't so bad. A few wagons, a few mules. My advisors say a friendly partner recovers faster than a bank.
You fought hard, and I respect that. Next time, let's have the fight in the market, where we both win.
I'm sending a bottle of decent wine to your camp. Consider it a thank you for keeping the eastern road calm.
A loss on the field, but I'm still ahead on goodwill. Call me when you're back in town, {player}. Ale's on me.

face.text: {player}, you fought a clean battle today. I lost the ridge, but I'd still trust you to escort my last wagon through the pass.
Well played on the field. I'm short a few carts, but I'm not short on respect, and that's worth more than wagons.
I came to bargain, not to brawl. You won the fight, so the least I can do is buy you supper once my men stop complaining.
Lost the ridge to a good friend. I'd rather lose to you than to anyone with a worse sense of fair play. Shall we talk prices?
Your formation was beautiful, {player}. Mine was a mess. Let me pay for the repairs, and we'll call it an education.
Ha! The field's yours, friend, but your standing with my caravans is still intact. Mind if I put in a bid for escort work?
You beat us fair and square, and I'd rather lose to someone honest than win against someone who cheats. Well done, {player}.
Next time we meet, I'll have a better scouting report. For now, let's just shake hands and count what's left in the cart.
Hard to be sore with someone who makes a battle this interesting. Lost the field, gained a story for the tavern.
{player}, I've half a mind to hire you for the next run. The men who beat me are the ones I want guarding my wagons.

global.text: Lost my wagons to {player} yet again. Third time. I'm starting to think the road has a favorite.
Another ambush, another ledger entry under {player}'s name. Bad for margins, and worse for my mood.
Every route I run ends with {player} waiting at the bend. Someone should sell tickets.
{player} has now cost me more than the tolls. I'm hiring bodyguards, and they are not cheap.
Sold out of ambush insurance after {player}'s last visit. Would not recommend the experience to anyone.
Note to self: {player} is not a trade partner, no matter how many times they offer a discount.
Lost {troop_count} crates' worth of goods to {player} today. Consider this my public complaint, filed in full.
Three losses to {player} now. I'm drawing up a formal grievance and it has footnotes.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, your ambush rate is starting to look like a tax. I'd rather pay it in gold than in cargo.
Third time now, {player}. Name a price to stop, or keep ruining my margins. Either way I'm keeping count.
Our wagons have met your blades again. Let's talk terms before the next one, I'm not made of coin.
I've priced in {player} as a fixed cost now. It's not a compliment, it's a warning.
Ambushed again, {player}? I've started wrapping my crates in thorns. Enjoy the splinters.
Next time I bring {troop_count} guards. Think of it as my counteroffer to your little hobby.
You keep taking my cargo and calling it a tax. Pick one word for it, please, I'm tired.
Still sore about the wagons, {player}. I'm not petty, I'm just keeping meticulous records.

global.text: Heard {player} had another win on the eastern road. Good for them, bad for the rest of us paying insurance.
Caravans running the eastern road should check in with someone before heading out. {player} knows the bends.
Three ambushes on the same stretch and the same name at the end. Just observing, not accusing.
Rumor: {player} is now the road's unofficial toll. Anyone know the rate?
Mixed feelings about the wagons lost this week. Prices will adjust. They always do.
Hauling goods is a gamble on good weather and worse company. Today the company was {player}.
Roads are getting expensive. If anyone wants a steady escort, I've got a list of what it costs.
I've stopped taking the bridge route. The timing never favors merchants when {player} is around.

whisper.text: Hello {player}. Three losses in a row now, nothing personal. Want to talk about a fair rate for passage?
I'm not angry, I'm running numbers. You've been the most consistent cost on my route, which is impressive.
Would you accept a retainer instead? Keep the roads quiet and I'll pay you a steady sum each month.
You've won three times. I'd like a rematch on paper, with contracts, and no swords involved.
Morning, {player}. Quick question: what's your price for leaving my caravan alone? Honest answer, please.
Let's be clear. I respect the consistency. I'm not sure I respect the method.
If your interest is in the road, I'd rather hire you than fight you. Think it over and send word.
Our last encounter cost me a crate of dyes. Put it on your tab, I'll let it go for a small favor.

global.text: Third time {player} has caught the bandits on my route. I'd call that a partnership, even if they don't know it yet.
Shoutout to {player} for keeping the eastern road clear. My prices there just got a lot more reasonable.
Lost to {player} again, and honestly? Best losing I've had all month. Wagons still intact, so I'm calling it a win.
If anyone's looking for a reliable escort, {player} has now earned my full recommendation. Discounts for friends.
{player} keeps beating me to the road's dangers. I'm starting to think they should be on my payroll.
The roads feel safer with {player} around. Good for trade, good for the wagons, good for my blood pressure.
Three ambushes, three rescues. {player} is making this route worth running again. Cheers!
Every time {player} steps in, the bandits lose and my margins gain. Honest deal, every time.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, you've beaten me three times now and somehow I still like you. Want to split a freight contract?
Lost to you again, {player}, but the cargo arrived in one piece. First round's on me next time we meet.
You keep catching the bandits before they catch me. I'd like to make that official. Retainer, fair rate, good terms?
Three losses and I still trust you with my wagons. That's either a compliment or a sign I need a better accountant.
Thanks for the escort, {player}. Not that it was an escort. Still, I owe you one, and I always pay my debts.
Keep catching the right bandits, {player}. We both profit when the roads stay open.
I'd lose to you a fourth time gladly if the freight stays safe. Want a cut of the next contract?
You beat me three times now, {player}. Let's make it four with a deal instead of a fight. Friendly rates, I promise.

global.text: {player} just cost me {troop_count} carts' worth of nerves. Next time, find a different road to rob.
Field battle with {player} done. Four wagons delayed, one mule sulking, and zero gold recovered. Lovely.
Reminder for traders: {player} charges a toll in blood. Plan your routes around that.
Sold {troop_count} sacks of grain last month and lost half to {player}'s ambush. Grim accounting.
Insurance agents now charge double for roads near {player}. Ask me how I know. Expensive lesson.
{player} thinks ambushes are a business model. Let me show them the ledger. It is not profitable.
Another skirmish with {player} and the caravan is two days behind schedule. Someone pay for that delay.
Dear {player}, your tactics cost me {gold} in lost cargo. I'm filing that under bad investments.
Hostile roads cut my weekly profit by a third. {player}, you are the reason I keep an armed guard now.
Seventeen mules, one broken axle, and {player} laughing at the far hill. Market forecast: grim.

whisper.text: {player}, you owe me {gold} in crates. Pay up or stay off my roads.
Your little ambush cost me a full wagon of dyed wool. I hope the hire was worth it.
I'll remember the field, {player}. Prices on the road go up every time you show your face.
Keep your bandits off my routes and we can talk prices. Until then, no discounts for you.
Lost {troop_count} guards to your spear line today. Not a sound investment, {player}.
A word, {player}: the next toll you dodge will come out of your own pocket.
Congratulations on the win. I've already sold the story to three inns at a markup.
You fought well, {player}, but my ledger doesn't care. I'm pricing you as a hazard now.
Hiring extra hands for convoys so you can't ambush us again. Costs more than your bribe, I'm sure.
Tell your crew the road fee just went up by {gold} per cart. Your ambushes made it necessary.

face.text: {player}, step back from my wagons. I counted {troop_count} of your men before the arrows started, and my account is bleeding.
You again? Every time we meet, I lose a wheel or a crate. Name your price to leave my road, and make it fair.
Walk away, {player}. My guards are paid to hold the line, and I'd rather not write off another cart today.
The fight's done, {player}. Lay your weapons down and we'll settle this with coin instead of more dead mules.
Your banner is the least welcome thing I've seen all week. Pack up and go, before I raise the toll on your head.
Lost {troop_count} carts' worth of goods to you. Forgive me if I don't offer you a seat at my fire.
{player}, I know what you are after. Gold, goods, or grudges. You won't find any of them on this road today.
Bloodied, bruised and out of coin, {player}? Good. Now you can understand what a bad week costs a trader.
I'd shake your hand, {player}, but my fingers are still sore from counting broken axles.
Stay on your side of the ridge and I'll stay on mine. My caravan has a schedule, and you've already ruined it.

global.text: Field battle near the crossing. Prices on the eastern road will move tomorrow, so watch the grain board.
Caravan losses on the ridge road this week. Whoever is raiding there, keep your distance from wagons.
Note to all carters: roads near the ford are contested. Pay for an escort or pay for a new axle.
Mixed results today on the hills. Lost some cargo, gained a little respect. Business as usual.
Salt and iron have both climbed since the skirmish. Expect shortages until the roads settle.
Friendly warning: a small band is working the northern route. Carry extra coin for the tolls.
Hauled {gold} worth of goods through the valley today without incident. Small mercies.
Battle lines are shifting near the bridge again. Keep wagons tight and eyes open on the ridge.
Anyone with spare wagons: the eastern road is quiet, but not for long. Price accordingly.
Did a bit of trading on the field today. Prices are fair, the company less so.

whisper.text: {player}, I'd like to keep this civil. Name a fair toll for passage and we'll both keep our carts.
No ill will from me, {player}, but I don't do trade with people who ambush first. Let's start over.
We fought, we stopped. Now tell me what you need, {player}, and I'll see if the price suits us both.
I have {troop_count} guards and an empty schedule. Want to talk terms, or shall we keep counting losses?
{player}, you're hard to read. Are you here to trade or to take? Let me know before the next wagon.
A warning, {player}: my carts go where the coin is. If that's your road, we can negotiate.
Fair fight, {player}. I'd rather charge you a fee than bury another good mule over a quarrel.
You'll find I'm patient with ledgers and wary of swords. Which one do you bring to my table?
Let's not make this a feud. A small safe-passage fee and both our teams go home richer.
My caravan master wants a clear answer, {player}. Are we still at war, or just at a price?

face.text: Hold your ground, {player}. I'm not after blood, only passage. Name your toll and we'll talk.
Good day, {player}. Your men fought well, so let's skip the sour faces and discuss a fair exchange.
We're done fighting for today. Keep your distance and we'll keep ours, and nobody has to bury anyone.
Easy with the blades, {player}. My guards are tired, my cart is bent, and I'd rather sell you bread than swing again.
I'll be honest with you, {player}. I don't know yet whether you're a customer or a problem. Tell me which.
The field's quiet now. If you want safe passage, the price is {gold} and a clean record.
You've got good discipline, {player}. Too bad your timing on the ridge cost my wagons a full day.
Pleasant as ever, {player}. Let's keep this quick, my oxen have had enough excitement for one afternoon.
I'll buy a truce if you're selling one. What's your asking price for keeping your bows down?
No more arrows today, {player}? Then let's find out whether we're trading partners or just tired enemies.

global.text: Shout out to {player} for holding the line today. Good sport in a skirmish, and a fine customer after.
{player} fought like a stubborn mule and still paid their tolls. That's my kind of rival.
Quick tip for carters: if {player} offers you an escort, take it. Fewer losses, better margins.
Lost a cart on the ridge today, but {player} was fair about it. Restitution and a handshake. Respect.
Our little skirmish with {player} ended with a deal on salt. Win-win, as far as I'm concerned.
If you want a reliable partner on the eastern road, {player} is the one to ask. Good word all round.
Field battle with {player} done, and I'm already planning the next convoy with them. Mostly kidding.
Credit to {player} for a clean fight and quick settlement. Caravans need more folk like that.
Good old {player}: they beat me on the hill, then bought my surplus grain at a fair price. Lovely.
Rumor has it {player} keeps the roads safer than any garrison. Not bad for a rival.

whisper.text: {player}, that was a proper battle. Next time we meet, bring your coin and I'll bring the good wine.
Well fought, {player}! You're the first rival I've enjoyed losing to. Let's talk about a joint shipment.
Stains on the cart wheels aside, my accounts have forgiven you. Your men made a fine show.
You beat my vanguard, {player}, so I'll offer you first pick of the spice shipment. Fair?
Drinks at the next waystation are on me, {player}. Let's compare notes on the northern prices.
Your tactics were sharp today. I'd like to put a retainer on them if you're open to escort work.
{player}, you're a worthy opponent. Even the ledger respects that kind of spine.
A small offer: half-price horses for anyone who fights as cleanly as you did today, {player}.
You won the field and I won a friend. Good trade, I'd say. Care to make it official?
Good fight, {player}. Let's keep this rivalry in the ledger and out of the mud.

face.text: {player}! That was a beautiful fight, and I'm still shaking off the dust. Wine at the next stop?
Look at you, {player}, all bloodied and grinning. Let's celebrate with a cup of wine and a fair contract.
Well done today, {player}. Your flanking worked, my wagons survived, and now I can offer you a job.
Ah, {player}, my favorite opponent. Tell me you brought your ledger, because I brought mine.
Stand down, friend, and let me buy you a meal. We'll talk escort rates over the stew.
I'll be honest, {player}, I wanted to win. But seeing you ride out makes me want a partnership instead.
That was a fine fight. My carts are battered, my pride is intact, and I still like you, {player}.
{player}, you've got the eye of a quartermaster. Walk with me to the crossing; I have an offer.
Good form on the hill, {player}! Shall we settle the stakes over bread, or is that bad for your reputation?
Rest your arm, {player}. We have three wagons and a cask of cider to split, and I'm inviting you to share.
You cost me a whole wagon of silk, {player}. Ransom is {gold}, and do not waste my time haggling.
Your sword made a fine argument, but my books still show a loss. Pay the {gold} and we shall call it even.
Bandits leave me alone and you leave me alone, yet here I am in chains. Typical luck on these roads.
I have met cheaper thieves than you, {player}, and they at least had the manners to bow first.
Every hour you keep me here costs me a fortune in missed caravans. Consider that before you smirk.
Ser, I will remember this face when I next set up my tolls. Expect to pay double on every crossing.
A fine victory, {player}. Shame it will not buy you a single bolt of cloth from {my_faction}.
Let me go, or I will tell every merchant between here and the coast that {player} is a rotten partner.
Right, I am your captive now. Shall we talk about {gold} for my release, or do you prefer to wait for my guards?
No need for the grim face. I have dealt with worse than you, and most of them paid on time.
I can see you are counting the coins in my purse already. Go on, the purse is lighter than you hope.
Chains are bad for the back and worse for trade. Let us settle this quickly, {player}, before the afternoon is gone.
I assume this is a ransom and not an insult. Tell me the sum, and I will tell you whether my factors can manage it.
Keep the rope tight if you must, but I need my ledgers at hand. A captive can still count, you know.
Whatever you think of me, the road to {my_faction} is long, and I am the only one who knows the shortcut.
If you mean to keep me, at least feed the horses. A dead merchant earns nobody anything, {player}.
Ha, well caught, {player}! I suppose a friend would name a fair price, so let us not make this ugly.
Captive or not, I still prefer you to the last brigand who took me. Shall we talk terms over supper?
You fight like a proper soldier, {player}. Pay me back with a favor on the northern road and we are square.
Honestly, I would sooner lose {gold} to you than to any tax collector. Let us say a fair ransom and part ways.
Take what you need from my wagon and send word to my agents. A partner who spares a merchant earns my trust.
No hard feelings, friend. Let me offer you a discount on my next shipment once I am back on my feet.
You have a good eye for an ambush, {player}. Perhaps we can make that talent pay on the caravan route.
Free me and I will tell {my_faction} you were gentle with me. That kind of word travels faster than any wagon.
An alliance with you? I'd sooner pay the tolls twice. Nothing personal, {player}, it's just bad for the books.
Ally with you so the next bandit ambush finds us both? No thank you. My caravans are not your shield.
You want my name on your banner? Last time that banner came with a burned wagon. Find another partner.
Hm. Tempting, but my ledger has no column for people who cost me money. Good day, {player}.
Alliance? Ha. I'd rather trade with {rival} than stand beside you, and at least they pay on time.
No alliance. I have seen what your friends do to a good road. Keep your swords off my route and we'll get along fine.
Every deal you offer comes with a hidden fee, {player}. I'm not signing a contract I can't read the back of.
I'll keep my coin and my counting house, thank you. Ask again when your reputation is worth more than your nerve.
An alliance, {player}? Let's start smaller. Sell me a cart of iron at a fair price and we'll see where it leads.
Interesting offer. I don't sign anything before I've checked the prices on three roads and two ledgers. Not today.
Ally? Depends what's in it for me. Right now the answer is nothing I can put in a wagon, so no.
I've seen partnerships end with empty purses and cold stares. I'll stick to deals that close in a day.
Mm, no. But I'm always buying wool and salt if you've got them. That's a relationship I can live with.
I don't take on partners who can't tell a toll gate from a tavern door. No alliance, but keep the trade open.
Honestly, the roads are dangerous enough without tying my name to yours. Let's keep it to coin and courtesy.
Not today, {player}. Come back when you've got a route that pays for itself and I'll hear you out properly.
Oh, I'd love to, {player}, truly. But I've already promised my caravan master I'd keep my coin and my contracts separate.
An alliance would be lovely, but my ledgers say no. Let's keep trading the way we do, and I'll throw in a discount.
Ah, you flatter me. I can't tie my wagons to yours, not yet. Buy me a drink later and we'll talk prices.
Partners is a big word for a merchant like me. How about you take first pick of my spice shipment instead?
I'm sorry, friend. Splitting profits with the best road guide in Ormerath is tempting, but I'd rather keep my independence.
No alliance this time, but you've earned a fair price on anything I haul. That's worth more than a banner, I promise.
Not this season, {player}. My partners would faint if I brought a sword-brother into the counting house.
I'd rather stay friends with a good customer than become allies with a bad debt. Shall we settle the wool order first?
Alright, an alliance it is. Pay your tolls on time and we will get along fine, {player}.
Fine by me. An alliance means fewer bandits on my roads, and that is worth more to me than your gold.
I accept. Let us see if this arrangement pays before we start calling each other friends.
Agreed. I will keep my caravans off your lands, and you keep your hands off my wagons. Simple trade.
A pact, then. I have made worse bargains and lived to count the profit, so let us try this one.
Yes, I accept. Write the terms down though, I have been burned by verbal promises on this road before.
Very well. Our roads will be safer with you on them, and safer roads mean cheaper grain for everyone.
I will sign on. Do not expect me to shout your name in the tavern just yet, but my wagons are yours to protect.
{player}! Of course I accept. Your name on my caravan contracts will do wonders for my reputation.
An alliance with you? Splendid. I was just complaining about bandits to my scribe, and now I have someone to complain with.
Accepted with a smile, friend. Tonight the first round is on me, and tomorrow we talk about the spice route.
Yes, yes, a thousand times yes. Between us we can undercut every toll gate from here to the river.
I accept, {player}. I was hoping you would ask before someone less pleasant beat you to it.
Good choice, friend. With you watching my back on the road, I can finally sleep through the night instead of counting coins.
Done! Our two names together will sell goods faster than any herald could shout them. Let us make some coin.
I accept gladly. I have a wagon of salt waiting on the east road, and I would rather it arrive with an escort of friends.
Fine, leave. Take your business somewhere else, I won't miss your custom one bit.
I'd say safe roads, but I'd rather not wish you luck. Go on, then.
Off you go, {player}. My ledger is happier without your name in it today.
Every coin you owe me still stands. Remember that on the road, won't you?
Walk on. I'll be watching the toll gate, and I doubt you'll find an easier price anywhere.
We're done. Don't come back expecting a discount, not after that stunt.
Go, then. The caravan won't weep over losing you, and neither will I, damn it.
Pleasant as ever, I see. Don't bother answering, I've heard enough. Mind the mud on the north track.
Hope the next merchant you meet remembers how you haggle.
I'll keep my goods out of your reach, thanks. Good day, and don't wave at me again.
Right, that's our business concluded. Safe travels, {player}, and mind the tolls on the river road.
Well, I've got a cart to load. Good day to you.
Thanks for stopping. Prices on the eastern route have gone up again, so keep that in mind.
Off to the next town, then. If you're heading that way, the bridge toll is two silver now.
I'm done talking shop for today. Watch your purse on the way, the roads are busier than usual.
Cheerio. I've a ledger to finish before the moon rises.
That's all I've got for you. Take care on the ridge, the last caravan lost two mules up there.
Good day. I've no interest in more haggling today, so I'll leave you to your journey.
Till next time, {player}. Don't wander too far from the main road, it's not as safe as it looks.
Hm, alright. Keep your coin close, the markets are half-empty this week.
Ah, {player}, always a pleasure! Come back soon, I've a fresh shipment of salt coming in next week.
Safe roads, my friend! Tell the stablemaster I said his mules owe me a favour.
You've been the best customer I've had all season, {player}. Don't be a stranger, I'll set your price aside.
Off you go then, and don't forget the spice route. Trust me, it's worth the detour.
Lovely doing business with you! If you hear of a fat wool order, send word straight away.
Good luck out there, {player}. I'd offer you a drink, but my last barrel went to a rather thirsty guard.
Right then, I'm off too. See you at the crossroads, and bring your appetite, I'll have a feast waiting.
You've made my whole week, honestly. Go on, the moon's rising and the good road gets dicey after dark.
Thank you kindly, {player}! Next time I'll have that ironwork you asked about, I promise.
Be well, friend! Remember my name at the inn, and you'll get first pick of the wagons.
Oh, it's you, {player}. Keep your hands where I can see them and your opinions to yourself. I'm just trying to move cargo.
Your reputation travels faster than your horse, {player}. Every toll I've paid this month was overpriced, and I'm holding you partly responsible.
I've got three guards and a fully loaded wagon, {player}. Go ahead and make a mistake. I'll happily tally the damages on your account.
Turn your party around, {player}. I'm not interested in a deal with someone who keeps spooking my drivers.
Ah, {player}. Last time we crossed paths, my salt went missing. I've been pricing your bruises ever since.
I don't trade with people who look at my cart like that, {player}. Find another road, and find another merchant while you're at it.
We're not buying what you're selling, {player}, and we're not selling you a thing either. Clear the path, please.
Mind your step, {player}. The last caravan that crossed your path lost two mules and a fair bit of profit. I'm keeping count.
Every time a wagon meets your party, the price of grain goes up a copper, {player}. I'm not in a generous mood today.
Stay on your side of the ford, {player}. My ledger has a page with your name on it, and it's not a page I want to add to.
Morning, {player}. Road's clear ahead, as far as I know. Just don't block the ford, it's bad for everyone's margins.
Good day, {player}. I'm carrying salt, wool and two barrels of wine. If you need any, ask nicely and we'll talk numbers.
Fair weather for travel, {player}. Keep your distance and we'll get along fine, and maybe we'll both make a little coin today.
Hello, {player}. Our wagons are on the same road, so we might as well keep the traffic moving and the prices honest.
{player}, I see your party's loaded down. Tolls at the next bridge have gone up again, so plan your purse accordingly.
Afternoon, {player}. My drivers are tired and my mule is sulking, so let's not make this encounter longer than it needs to be.
Lovely day for a delivery, {player}. If you're headed toward the market town, the northern road is safer than the old pass.
{player}, your party's cart looks sturdy. Mine's a bit bent from a pothole, but it still turns a profit, which is what matters.
Greetings, {player}. I've got no quarrel with anyone who pays their tolls on time, so keep that in mind as we pass.
Hail, {player}. Caravan business is slow this season, so if you're carrying anything worth moving, I'd like to hear about it.
{player}! Good to see you on the road. I've got fresh spices, and I'll knock a few coins off for an old friend.
Ser {player}, what a pleasant surprise. I was just reckoning how much I owe you for that last good turn on the mountain pass.
There you are, {player}! My cart's a little heavy with ale today, so come share a cup and tell me what you're hauling.
Well met, {player}. You've got that look of someone who can turn a profit, and I've got just the wagon to help with that.
{player}, my favourite partner in trade. Let's compare notes on prices before the next town's markets open up.
Safe travels, {player}! Thanks again for keeping the bridge clear last week. My profits are better for it, and I'm not forgetting that.
Ah, {player}, I'd know that party's banner anywhere. If you're short on supplies, I'll give you a fair rate and call it neighbourly.
Greetings, friend {player}! I've been meaning to find you about a trade route. A cut for both of us, if you're willing to hear it out.
{player}, you're a sight for weary eyes. The roads have been rough, but a wagon with your party's name on it always brings me some luck.
Good timing, {player}! I've got a spare crate of tools and an honest price, and I'd rather sell it to someone I trust.
Threats again? Fine. My toll gate costs {gold} to pass, and I'd rather you pay it than bleed on my good cart.
You want my purse, I want my cart back in one piece. Pick whichever you can afford to lose, {player}.
I've buried better customers than you for less trouble. Name your ransom and let's get it over with.
Every time someone like you stops me, the road gets a little more expensive. You're making it my problem.
Mark this day, {player}. You just cost me a route, a bodyguard's wages and my good temper all at once.
Hm. A brave tongue for someone standing in the mud. I'll take {gold} and you may keep the rest of your dignity.
Keep your steel sheathed and your hands where I can see them. Haggling is still an option, sadly for you.
I'd call you a bandit, but bandits at least charge fair rates. Pay up, or walk your empty road home.
Do you know what a wagon guard costs per week? Now add your nonsense to that bill, and we'll see who laughs.
Bad luck on your end, not mine. Hand over {gold} and I'll pretend this little scene never happened.
Threatening a merchant on the open road. Bold. Let's talk numbers before either of us does something we regret.
I can give you {gold} for your trouble, or you can wander off with nothing. Both are fair in their own way.
Demands are cheap, {player}. Coin is what I deal in. Tell me what you actually need and we'll see.
I've no quarrel with you yet. Make it worth my while and I'll forget this moment ever happened.
Surrender my cart? Ah, you want an auction. The opening bid is {gold}, and I won't be pushed higher.
Let's be reasonable. You have a blade, I have a ledger. One of us is going to walk away richer.
Interesting opening offer. I'll counter with a quarter of what you asked and a warm meal at the next inn.
Pay the toll and we're done. Argue and we both lose a day, and days are the only thing I can't buy back.
Nobody's taking the wagon today. But I might take a small loss on the goods if you'd hear me out.
You're not the first to stop me here, and you won't be the last. Name your price and keep your temper.
Oh, {player}, you always know how to make a poor merchant sweat. Fine, you get the usual discount on my toll.
Ha! Threatening me over a barrel of salted fish? You're going to make me miss my own shop opening.
If you must rob me, {player}, at least do it at the market price. Friends pay a little less, you know.
We both know you're just testing the cart's springs. Take {gold} off the price and I'll pretend I was scared.
Put that scowl away, my favorite customer. I'll trade you a fresh pie for a ride down the road together.
You're a terrible bandit and a wonderful buyer. Let's skip the threats and talk about what you'd like to buy.
Now then, {player}, you've had your fun. Shall we settle things over tea, or do you still want the wagon?
Honestly, you could have just asked nicely. I'd have sold you the cart for {gold} and a good word.
Easy, easy! Your charm is wasted on a wagon, but I'll gladly give you a loyal customer's rate.
You know I can't stay angry at you for long. Half the coin, a cup of cider, and we're square again.
Your offer is insulting, {player}. I'd sooner sell my cart wheels for kindling than take {gold} for that.
Hmm, {player}. The last time we traded you tried to shortchange me. I'm counting my coins twice this time.
I'll hear your deal, but keep your hands off my crates. Last time a bargain with you cost me a good mule.
Another bad bargain from you, {player}? Fine. Make it worth my while or take your wares back to {town}.
Your price is a joke. Come back when your purse is heavier than your opinion of yourself.
I've no patience for haggling today, {player}. Name a number I can believe or we're done here.
You want a deal from me, after you cheated my caravan at the ford? Bold of you, but I'll listen. Briefly.
Trading with you is like paying a toll to a bandit. I'll take {gold}, but I'm writing it down so I never forget.
A deal, you say? Let's see what you've got. Plenty of offers have come down this road and most of them were smoke.
Show me the goods first, {player}. Then we'll talk about {gold}. Prices in {town} have been jumping all week.
The roads are eating my profits in tolls lately, so your offer had better be fair. Go on.
I don't mind a bit of haggling. Just be quick about it, the sun's moving and so is my wagon.
Put your proposal on the table and I'll tell you whether it's worth my time. Most aren't.
Hm. {gold} is more than I expected you'd offer, so I'm listening, though I'm not sold yet.
Between the bandits and the toll men, every trade is a gamble. Tell me what you're offering and we'll see.
Sounds reasonable on paper. Paper is cheap though, ser. Show me the coin and the cargo before we shake.
Ah, {player}, you always make a morning worth it. Let's talk numbers over a warm cup.
For you, {player}, I'll cut my margin to the bone. Consider it an investment in a friendship that pays dividends.
Good offer. Better than the one I got from {town}'s grain factor, which is a sad thing to admit.
You've got a head for business, and I've got a wagon that needs a buyer. Shall we shake on {gold}?
I was hoping you'd come by. Let's make the deal, and then I'll buy you a drink at the next waystation.
Your terms are fair, friend, so fair I'm half suspicious. Still, I'll take them before I change my mind.
If anyone can turn a dull caravan into a profit, it's you, {player}. Count me in for a share.
Deal! Now let's get this cargo loaded before the rain ruins the spices and my good mood along with them.

global.text: That skirmish cost me two carts and a mule. Worth it if the road's clear now.
Rough fight out there, but the south road should be safer for hauling salt again.
Good that the bandits are gone. Now somebody please fix the toll at the bridge.
Won the field, lost a wagon wheel. Anyone selling spare axles at a fair price?
Battle's over. Prices in the market will sag by morning once the troops move on.
Glad the fighting ended. Hard to haggle when half the town is still counting its dead.
{troop_count} soldiers marched past my stall today. Feed bills alone will ruin me.
Roads clear again. Keep your swords sheathed on the trade route, and your coin purses close.

whisper.text: Fought beside you today, {player}. Don't expect a favour for it, but I won't forget.
Your line held well out there. Shame about the cost. Want to talk about shared shipping?
We both got paid in blood today. I'd rather get paid in gold next time, if you agree.
Thanks for the help at the ford, {player}. Keep your receipts, I keep mine.
That was a messy win. Still, a win is a win. Let's see who buys the captured mules.
I'm not in the habit of thanking people, but the flank was tight. Nice work, {player}.
Captured supplies are being sold at the camp tonight. Fair shares if you show up early.
We stood together long enough to win. Now let's stand apart again before I start owing favours.

face.text: Well fought, {player}. Our wagons are still in one piece, which is more than I expected today.
Ah, you're the one who covered my left side. I'll remember that, though my accountant won't.
The field is ours. Now, if you have a spare horse to sell, I'm listening.
Good to see you standing. Bandits and battles both hurt my margins, so let's keep the road quiet.
Our side took the hill, and I took three barrels of wine from the enemy camp. Honest trade, I say.
That was a long afternoon. My feet hurt, my coin purse is light, but at least the road is open.
Do you smell that? Smoke and cheap ale. Victory always smells like a bad market day.
Fine work out there. If you ever need carts moved safely, my rates are reasonable and my patience is short.

global.text: Huge thanks to everyone who held the ford today. Caravans can roll again, drinks on me at the inn!
Great win, folks. {player} carried the left flank like a seasoned guard. Respect.
Our battle won, the road's open, and salt prices should finally drop. Best day in weeks.
Shoutout to the lads who fought off {enemy_faction} at dawn. Nothing beats a clean victory and full wagons.
Need escorts for next week's run? Anyone who fought today gets a discount. Loyalty pays.
Victory pricing: every blade sharpened in my shop this week is half off. Spread the word!
{player}, that flank charge was something. I'll be telling this story at every market from here on.
Thank you all for the fight. Caravan rates drop for anyone who shows up at the next muster. Trust me, I'm a merchant.

whisper.text: You were brilliant out there, {player}. Want a share of the captured wine? I'll give you a fair cut.
Thanks for watching my back. Next time I'm hauling, you're first on my list for escort work.
Honest question: would you ride with my caravan next week? I'll cover the tolls and the food.
That charge saved my best wagon. I owe you, and I always pay my debts, one way or another.
Between us, the enemy's horses are going cheap now. Come by and I'll give you a friend's price.
I'm glad you were there today, {player}. A good partner is worth more than any spare crossbow.
Drinks are on me tonight if you're free. Plenty to celebrate, and a few deals to discuss.
You fought like someone who understands business: you know when to push and when to hold. Let's partner up.

face.text: {player}! That was quite the fight. Come see me, I've got a crate of spices you'll be glad to own.
Ser, you held that bridge like it owed you money. I like that. Let's talk about a regular route.
Victory suits you, {player}. I'd offer a handshake, but my hands are full of captured silver.
We made a good team out there. Let's keep it going. I'll pay for the next round and the next run.
I saw you cover the cart when the arrows flew. You've earned a discount, and perhaps a bigger share.
Thanks for fighting for the road, {player}. Next market day the first cup is mine.
You know, I hate war, but you made it profitable. Remind me to put you on the company payroll.
Fine work, friend. Our {troop_count} soldiers would have been scattered without you. Let's celebrate properly.

global.text: {fief} is ours now, and the toll ledgers are already open. Caravans can roll in by dusk.
With {my_faction} holding the gate at {fief}, the roads should be safer for wagons. Bring your goods, ser.
Took {fief} with less fuss than I expected. The brewers there will want fair prices for their stock.
Anyone with grain to sell, {fief} needs it badly. Prices in the market square are already climbing.
Good riddance to {enemy_faction}'s tax men in {fief}. Their tolls were robbing every cart on the road.
Hope {enemy_faction} enjoyed their stay in {fief}. Their salt tolls were criminal, frankly.
Captured {fief} and now I have to rebuild the inn ledgers from scratch. Lovely work, truly.
Wars come and go, but a well-run market outlasts them all. {fief} will be trading again by spring.
Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} means the northern road is finally open. Caravans, here we come.
Tolls on the {faction} crossing should drop now that the treaty is signed. Finally, a number that makes sense.
Peace with {faction} means fewer bandits hiding behind old war banners. Shame it took this long to happen.
Years of war and iron still kept climbing. Peace is the first good news my ledger has seen in ages.
I'll raise a cup to peace with {faction}. Strictly for the trade routes, of course, not the wine.
Armies come and go, but a road that stays open earns the same coin every season. Wiser than any sword.
Pricing on {faction} wool just shifted with the treaty. Anyone else want in before the rush hits?
Hope this peace holds. A treaty that breaks by spring is worse for margins than a war we all expected.
Siege lines around {fief} and nobody's buying a single crate. Wonderful for my margins, said no merchant ever.
Our grain convoy is stuck outside {fief} because of this siege. Who pays for the lost days, exactly?
Every lord with a siege engine fancies themselves a strategist. Meanwhile my tallow sits rotting in a cart.
Forty wagons idle at the {fief} gate. Forty! I've started calculating how many lost weeks a siege costs.
Trade routes to {fief} are closed. Lift the siege or name a toll I can afford to pay, please.
Haggling is fine. Sieges are not. Shall we agree my wagons pass freely again before the week is out?
I've already priced in a winter without a working wall at {fief}. Really hope this was worth the margins, {player}.
Salt, grain, wool, all stuck behind one camp outside {fief}. Someone explain the logic to me, because I can't find it.

whisper.text: Your siege just cost me three contracts, {player}. I'm not angry, I'm just keeping accounts.
Lift the siege and I'll forget the lost shipment. Refuse and I start pricing your supply line.
Strange thing, {player}. Every siege I've watched ends with someone paying for the wall repairs. Usually not the besiegers.
Walls can be repaired. Lost trust takes longer. Consider that before your next ram swings, {player}.
A ledger doesn't forget, {player}. Your name now sits next to 'siege' and 'losses' in mine.
My caravan guards are already talking about hiring out to someone less likely to start a fight. Thanks for that.
Tell me your price for ending this, {player}. Be honest, and I'll be honest back.
If this is about an old grievance, say it plainly. Sieges are a terrible way to settle accounts, {player}.

global.text: Heard there's a siege at {fief}. Anyone know if the gates will be open for trade by next week?
Siege at {fief} again. Dried fish jumped in price overnight. Watch your purses, friends.
Not taking sides here. I just want my wagons to reach {fief} without a soldier poking at them.
Quiet markets make for quiet nerves. If the siege at {fief} ends, I'll have stock ready at fair rates.
Sieges come and go, but the roads remain. Does anyone know which way the grain trade is leaning?
Whoever is at {fief}'s walls, please mind the bridge. It's the only crossing my carts can use.
I've seen nine sieges this year. Each one costs me about a week of sales. Try not to make it ten.
Keeping my head down and my accounts open. Once the siege at {fief} wraps up, I'll be first with a cart.

whisper.text: Heard about the siege at {fief}, {player}. Still interested in a fair share of my wool once the gates open?
No grudges from me, {player}. I'd just like to know when my supply carts can safely move again.
You're camped outside my town, {player}, which makes this a bit awkward. Shall we talk terms over tea?
Friendly warning: every day at {fief} costs me about forty gold in spoiled goods. Can we keep it short?
I don't care who wins, {player}. I care who pays the toll afterward. Interested in a quick arrangement?
Sieges are bad for everyone's books, {player}. Mind telling me how long you plan to keep this up?
If you're short on supplies outside {fief}, I can sell you bread at a fair rate. Business is business.
No need to glare at my caravan, {player}. We're merchants, not generals. Let's see what the market says.

global.text: {player} lost {troop_count} troops in one afternoon. Every road they use gets pricier now.
Watched {player}'s whole host march into the ditch. Pricey boots, those. Shame about the boots.
Another army gone, and {player} still wants tolls on the north road. Remarkable.
Those {troop_count} men were worth more alive as porters. Ask any caravan master.
Lost {troop_count} soldiers and half the wagons. Honest question: who insures that?
Tallied the losses for {player}: wagons, grain, {troop_count} men. Bad books all round.
Good riddance to the inflated war budget. {player} bought a funeral, not an army.
Expect nobody to sell {player} a single spear on credit after that.

whisper.text: Heard about your {troop_count} lost men, {player}. Terrible for everyone's margins, yours included.
Don't come to my stalls asking for credit, {player}. Cash only until your coffers recover.
Your defeat cost me two wagons on the eastern road. Send a bill if you like, I'll send one back.
I'm not refusing to trade with you, {player}, but my prices just went up. Consider it a tax on bad generals.
Lost {troop_count} soldiers and you still haggle like a winner. Admirable, almost.
Caravans are already rerouting around your lands, {player}. Nothing personal. Quite personal, actually.
Hire fewer swords next time, {player}. Protection money is a poor investment when the protection loses.
Sorry for your losses, {player}. Not sorry enough to sell you grain at a discount.

global.text: {player}'s army broke against the ridge. Anyone know if the grain prices will follow?
Lost {troop_count} men and the supply carts? Expensive lesson, that.
Fresh graves outside the pass mean fewer hands on the roads. Hauling costs rise again.
Armies cost more to lose than to keep. {player} is finding that out at full price.
Mercenary contracts just got harder to fill, thanks to {player}'s recent misfortune.
Heard {troop_count} soldiers fled the field. Whatever the cause, I'd hire wagon guards before the next march.
Military routes are pricey enough without battles. Keep an eye on the wool market, friends.
Defeat or not, {player} still owes the carters for last month. Just saying.

whisper.text: Heard the battle went badly, {player}. If you need supplies moved, my wagons are available at the usual rate.
Sorry about the defeat. Losing {troop_count} men is hard on everyone's ledgers.
Your scouts should have taken the lower road. I'd know, I paid their tolls twice.
Thinking of rebuilding? Horses are cheaper this month, and I'll throw in a saddle.
A bad week for your troops, {player}. Shall we talk about insurance on the next caravan?
No hard feelings for the losses, but the road tax is still due on schedule, {player}.
I could sell you replacement armour, {player}, but only if you pay up front this time.
Ouch. Lost most of your force? My sympathies, and my spare carts are yours for a fair fee.

global.text: Brave push by {player} at the ridge, even if the army didn't hold. Next campaign, I'm sponsoring.
{player} lost {troop_count} men and still shook my hand afterward. Good sport, that one.
Feel for {player} after the rout. Half my wagons were lost in that mess too.
Rebuilding an army is a tidy business. {player} knows where to buy good steel.
Losses hurt, but {player}'s reputation for paying debts will carry them through.
Shoutout to {player} for retreating in good order. Saved a fair few carts.
I'd bet on {player} making the money back by spring. Cheers to a comeback!
Put the coins back in your purse, {player}. Your next order's on the house, don't argue.

whisper.text: Sorry about the army, {player}. Come by the stalls, I've got a discount on horses for loyal customers.
Losing {troop_count} men is rough. Want me to float you some credit till the harvest?
That retreat was smart, {player}. Keep the wagons safe and I'll keep the prices fair.
You're still my favourite client, {player}, defeat or no defeat. Lunch on me?
Honest question: will you be hiring escorts for the next run, {player}? I know good ones.
Tough day, {player}. Rest up, then drop by. I've got a shipment of helmets that'd suit you.
Your fighters held the road better than most. Let's talk about a retainer contract.
Buy you a drink, {player}? Our next deal is going to need a clear head and a full purse.

global.text: Ran off before the first swing. Very efficient. My ledger is still waiting on that coin, though.
Fled my caravan mid-stance. Someone should tell them the road only gets longer from here.
Fifteen wagons of goods and {player} sprints for the hedgerows. Nobody here is surprised.
Turned tail at the first sign of steel. Every toll post will hear about this, I promise.
Running from a fight over a few crates? Bad margins for your reputation, friend.
Took to the trees the moment we formed up. Cowardice is not a line item I'd invest in.
Scattered like spilled grain the moment my guards drew. Keep the road, then. Chase your own shadows.
Wagons tied, guards ready, and {player} vanishes into the brush. Expect no more invitations to trade.
Afraid of a bit of honest bargaining with a blade? Every merchant on Ormerath is watching now.
Ran. Good. Next time I'll bring a bigger purse and you'll have less room to flee.

whisper.text: Ran off like a spooked mule, {player}. You cost me a fine afternoon and a fair bit of profit.
Retreating in that direction is bad for your reputation. Roads here remember who turns tail.
Clever flight. Still, my caravan lost a day waiting on you. I don't forget lost days.
Hope the bolt of cloth you were hoping to sell is worth the hedgerow you hid behind.
No swordplay today? Fine. I'll be sure to charge you double whenever our paths cross again.
You ran from my wagons like they owed you money. Lesson learned: I will still come collect.
Dashing off mid-meeting is rude, {player}. Next time, at least leave a note with the bill.
I'll assume the hedgerow was a better bargain than the one I offered. Enjoy the mud.
Tell your fellows that running from a caravan costs more than the goods you saved, in the end.
We'll meet again on a road of my choosing, {player}. Pray your purse is heavier by then.

global.text: Saw a few folk bolting off the north road today. Nothing to see, just keep your wares close.
{player} took the sensible route and left my caravan a clear road. Smart move, however you slice it.
Anyone else notice the road toll shrinks whenever people decide not to fight? Just a thought.
Caravan turned around for a skirmish that never happened. Time lost is coin lost, friends.
Ran into a skittish traveller who bolted before the first horn. Everyone pack light and move quick.
Standoffs on the open road cost more than they're worth. Wise choice to walk away, {player}.
No blood, no bargains, no harm. Gotta love a road that stays quiet for once.
Caravan's fine, merchants are fine, and somebody's pride is probably bruised. Business as usual.
Tip for the lot of you: a decent escort is cheaper than a grudge. Ask me about the rates.
Seems like the roads are getting twitchy. If you're hauling salt, do it with company.

whisper.text: Good instincts today, {player}. Clear road means no losses on either side, which suits me fine.
Did you need the cart I was driving or was it just a fright? Either way, no hard feelings from me.
No fight, no trouble. Just a note: if you're heading toward the coast, mind the toll stones.
Quick feet, sharp eyes. Keep those and you'll outlast most traders. Good luck on the road.
I'd rather trade than tangle. If you ever want to talk prices instead of swords, my door is open.
Rattled your nerves, did we? Fair enough. Wagons are expensive to lose, so I understand the caution.
Kept the goods, kept your skin. A solid trade for a morning's work, I'd say.
Your escape was tidy. If you ever need a shoulder on a rough stretch, send word.
No need for a chase. I've got a route to keep, and you've got wherever you were rushing to.
Retreating was sensible. A brawl over a wagon costs more than most trades bring in. Think on it.

global.text: Shoutout to {player} for ducking out before the blades came out. Best call I've seen all week!
{player} just proved that a quick exit beats a bad fight. Drinks on my coin when we next meet.
Can't blame anyone for avoiding a scrap over a few sacks of grain. Keep your purses light, friends.
Glad to see {player} walked away clean. Loyal customers are worth more than any single bolt of cloth.
Heard {player} outran a whole band of brigands this morning. Now that's a sales pitch I can use.
Smart retreat from {player} today. Not every road needs a crossing; some just need a bit of patience.
Wagons safe, goods intact, and {player} keeps a clean record. My kind of partner, honestly.
Nobody dies over a dye batch, folks. {player} knew that, and I respect the call.
Good on {player} for trusting their feet over bravado. Caravans love a sensible escort.
Shoutout to {player}: escaped the mess and still wants to buy salt from me. Legend.

whisper.text: You're a sight for sore eyes after that skirmish that wasn't, {player}. Come by the stall, first cup's on me.
Good call bolting, {player}. I'd rather keep you as a customer than as a casualty. Care to discuss salt?
No hard feelings about the scramble. Let's make it up with a discounted route on your next trip, {player}.
Next time you're on the south road, I'll have a cart with your name on it. Discount included.
Honestly, running was smarter than standing your ground. I'd rather trade with you than bury you.
Saw your heels kick up dust. Wise. Want to split the cost of an escort on the way back?
Thought you were a goner there, {player}. Glad the road didn't win this round.
You've got a head for the road. I could use that on the next run, if you're interested.
Shame our paths crossed under those circumstances. Let's sit down over prices when you're rested, {player}.
Quick feet, clear head, and no shame in it. Good instincts, {player}. Let's talk business soon.

global.text: {player} got {fief} handed over by the ruler? Lovely. Tolls there will be fun to raise.
Nothing says fair market like a fief given out by favour. Hope {fief}'s roads stay safe for everyone else.
Congratulations to {player} on {fief}. I'll be counting the coin I didn't make there, thank you very much.
Caravans will route around {fief} from now on. Someone should tell the ruler a town without trade is just a ruin.
Another castle for {player}, another ledger I'd like to see audited. Just curious what the books look like.
Favours from the crown don't make a market. Prices in {fief} will tell the real story, mark my words.

whisper.text: Heard the ruler gave you {fief}. Enjoy it, {player}. I'll be sending my caravans the long way round.
Pleased for you, truly. Pity my offer for the {fief} salt rights got ignored in favour of a friend.
You got {fief} for free and I paid a fortune to get near it. Call me jealous. I'm not wrong though.
Don't expect me to bring you any goods from now on, {player}. Your tolls already cost me a fortune.
Every merchant in {fief} is wondering what you'll charge them. I'd start a list of who to avoid.
Enjoy the title, {player}. Titles don't fill a warehouse. Rude of the crown not to ask me first.

global.text: New lord in {fief}. Let's see if the tolls stay sane or the roads go quiet. Could go either way.
{fief} changed hands by royal decree. Traders, check your prices before you make the trip.
Who holds {fief} matters less to me than whether the bridge tolls hold steady. Keep it fair.
Fresh grant for {fief} means fresh rules. Anyone know what the new lord plans for the market square?
Heard {player} has {fief} now. Caravans will still go where the coin is good, whoever's flag flies.
Rulers come and go, but a good road is forever. Let's see whether {fief} keeps its roads open.

whisper.text: Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Let me know what your tolls look like before I unload any wool there.
So the crown gave you {fief}. Fine by me, as long as the road fees don't double overnight.
Heard you're taking over {fief}. Care to share your plans for the market? Helps me plan my routes.
I'll be watching {fief} closely under your rule. Good trade keeps everyone rich. Bad trade gets noticed.
Don't mind me looking over your new books, {player}. Every lord in {fief} gets the same look from me.
A castle and a title. Impressive, {player}. Now what's the price of a safe escort through {fief}?

global.text: Good news for trade: {player} now holds {fief}. Expect cheaper salt and fewer bandits on those roads.
Raise a cup to {player}, new lord of {fief}! My caravans will be the first ones through the gates.
{fief} with a fair lord at the helm? Now that's a market worth investing in. Well done, {player}.
Anyone with goods to sell, head to {fief}. {player} is known to pay honest prices. Good for business.
Half the realm was jealous of {player} this week, and I'm happy to be the other half. {fief} needs this.
Good for {fief}, good for the roads, good for my ledger. Long may {player} hold that castle.

whisper.text: Congratulations on {fief}, {player}! Want first pick of my spices when your stores are up? Friends' rates.
Proud of you for getting {fief}. If you need a supplier for the new walls, I have contacts.
I knew the crown would see sense eventually. Let's sit down over a drink and talk about {fief}'s trade.
Well earned, {player}. Shall I send a caravan to {fief} to restock? First shipment's on me.
{fief} is in good hands now. I'd gladly escort your next delivery if you ever need one, no charge.
A castle is a lot of upkeep, {player}. Tell me what you need and I'll find you a deal.

global.text: {player} swore to {my_faction}? Fine. Let's see if the oath lasts longer than my patience.
Another sword on the payroll, another mouth to feed out of my tolls. Wonderful.
Had {player} down as a bandit last month. Now they're family. Trade's a strange old game.
Hope {player} actually pays the tariffs this time. The last oath-taker didn't, and I'm still annoyed.
Swearing loyalty is cheap. Paying road fees on time is the real test, {player}.
{my_faction} takes anyone now, apparently. Keep lowering the bar and my caravans start asking questions.

whisper.text: Heard about the oath, {player}. I'll be watching your tolls closer than your banners, I promise.
Don't expect a discount for swearing in. You still owe me for that wagon you 'borrowed'.
Congratulations on joining. I'll be the one counting every coin that passes your gate, friend.
Oaths don't change my prices, {player}. Ambush me again and I'll bill {my_faction} for the damages.
Let's be honest, you swore for the protection. Just remember who pays for the roads you walk.
Still not sure you're trustworthy. Prove it with a fair toll and I might warm up. Maybe.

global.text: New oath taken today at the gate. Roads should be a bit calmer if the new banners hold.
{player} is with {my_faction} now. Ask me in a month whether the tolls changed.
Fresh allegiances mean fresh contracts. Wagons moving out of {my_faction} lands by dawn.
Saw {player} take the oath. Doesn't change my margins much, but I'll allow some hope.
Good to see more hands signing up for {my_faction}. Fewer bandits, fewer headaches for everyone.
Watching who swears to {my_faction} and who sticks around. Business always tells you the truth eventually.

whisper.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Oaths are fine, but I'll judge you by how you handle a fair price.
Congratulations on the oath. If you need a wagon for the new post, I can offer a sensible rate.
Swearing in is the easy part. Keeping the caravan routes open is what really earns respect here.
Well, {player}, the banners are changing. Care to talk about grain prices before the next market?
I'll keep my ledger open for you. Show up on time with the tolls and we'll get along well enough.
Nice to have you on the books now, {player}. Let's see how the new allegiance affects your purse.

global.text: Huge welcome to {player}, who just swore to {my_faction}! Drinks on the caravan tonight, first round free.
Good news for everyone: {player} is ours now. Roads grow safer when honest folk stand together.
Cheers to {player} for joining {my_faction}. My best salt contracts are already looking brighter.
{player} just became a pillar of {my_faction}. I'd call that a very profitable day for us all.
Let's raise a cup to {player}! Stout hearts keep the trade routes open and the coin flowing.
Welcome aboard, {player}. Come find me at the market and we'll settle the first deal of many.

whisper.text: Glad you swore in, {player}! I've got a shipment of dyed wool that could use a trustworthy escort.
Welcome to {my_faction}! Drop by when you have a moment, I'll give you my best price on horses.
So pleased you chose us, {player}. Honest oaths make honest trade, and honest trade makes me smile.
Congrats, {player}. I'll knock ten percent off your next order as a welcome gift. Don't tell the others.
Lovely to have you with {my_faction}. Shall we discuss a partnership on the northern route?
Welcome, {player}! With you on our side the roads will be safer and my ledgers will be happier. Win-win.

global.text: {player} switched to {faction} and took my best contacts with them. Every route I trust now costs double.
Left {my_faction} for {faction}? Fine. Next time you need a loan, go ask your new friends for the interest rate.
Heard {player} is hawking {faction}'s banners now. Shame. Nobody haggles like a turncoat, they just undercut.
Every caravan route {player} used to guard is now a toll gate. Keep your swords, I'll keep my purse.
Loyalty is the cheapest thing on the market and {player} just sold it at a loss. Terrible margins, really.
Reminder to all traders: {player} walks out on contracts when a better offer shows up. Price your trust accordingly.

whisper.text: You knew what my caravans meant to {my_faction}, {player}. Switching sides cost you more than a stall, mark that.
Don't bother asking for my horses now. I don't sell to people who sell out their own.
I've already moved your credit to the bottom of my ledger. Not spite, just bookkeeping.
Half my wagons are rerouted around {faction}'s land now, thanks to you. Enjoy the detour in your new colors.
Will I trade with you again? Maybe, if the price is high enough. Don't expect a warm welcome, ser.
Ser, I'm not angry, I'm just writing you down as a bad risk. Ink's cheap, memories last longer.

global.text: Heard {player} moved over to {faction}. Hope the new roads pay better, because the old ones were fine.
Anyone know whether {faction} is actually paying their guards this month, or is it all promises again?
Defection season again. Prices move with it, so buy your salt before the next announcement.
{player} has a new banner and a new supply line. Watching where the grain goes next will tell me plenty.
Switching factions is like switching carts mid-journey: you lose time and half your cargo. Just saying.
Whatever {player} chose, the market doesn't care. Wool is still wool and {my_faction} still pays on time.

whisper.text: Heard you signed with {faction} now, {player}. Still interested in the horse route, or are those contracts off?
No grudges here, but I'll be checking receipts twice before any deal from now on.
If you still want the usual rate on salt, ask me directly. The old terms stand until I hear otherwise.
Your new friends will want the same goods I sell, so expect a little competition, ser. Nothing personal.
I'm not sure which side to watch now, so tell me straight: are we still trading or not?
A word of advice: keep your old accounts open. Loyalty is a lot easier to rebuild than a bad reputation.

global.text: Some folk call {player}'s move to {faction} a betrayal. I call it a bold pivot. Good luck with the new books.
Changing banners is no crime. Most of the best deals I ever made started with someone switching sides.
Off to {faction} with {player}? Remember, the best margins still come from the people who ask nicely.
Anyone still trusting {player} with a fair price on dyed wool? Most of us will, trade is trade.
Watch the roads, folks. A friend who changes banners still knows the best inns, so I'll keep sending my people their way.
Between us, I'd rather trade with a flexible ally than a loyal fool. Good luck, {player}, and mind the tolls.

whisper.text: Don't let the nasty posts get you down, {player}. I'd still happily split a caravan route with you.
You're still welcome at my stall. Money well spent on a partner, and you were always good for a fair price.
Going over to {faction} doesn't change my opinion of you. Want to talk about horses before you leave?
I'll be honest, the gossip is loud. I'm more interested in whether your new supplier pays on time.
Good luck settling in with {faction}. Send me a message when you need a reliable hauler, I'll give you my best rate.
Don't worry about the hard words from the old crowd. Traders remember who paid their bills, and you always did.

global.text: {player} burned {village} to the ground. Nice work, really. Every merchant on the east road just got a little poorer.
Lost the whole wool harvest in {village} to {player}'s torches. Prices in the market will feel that.
Fire at {village} means no grain for three towns. Somebody tell {player} the bread price is on them now.
Anyone planning to trade near {village}? Stay away from {player} until the road is safe. Learned that the hard way.
Insurance does not cover arson by {player}. Who knew. Every caravan will now pay double for escorts.
Ask me again why I hate open raiding. {village} is the reason, and {player} is the name on the ashes.
Raids like {player}'s cost more than the loot is worth. Ledger says red, and I am keeping score.
{village} is ash. Traders, route your wagons around {player}'s band. I am not joking about the tolls.

whisper.text: {player}, you burned {village} and my profits with it. I will remember the smell of that smoke.
Rude. Very rude. I had a shipment of salt waiting in {village}. Now I have ash and a grudge.
I could have sold you horses at a fair price, {player}. Now you can buy them from someone else at my markup.
Expect my caravans to avoid your roads from now on. I will not be trading with you until this is made right.
Burning {village} was a poor investment, {player}. Worst return I have seen all season, and I have seen a few.
Do not message me asking for a discount. The only discount you will get is the one I give to the road guards.
{player}, I am writing down every wagon you have cost me. The total is long and it is not getting shorter.
Stay out of {village}'s market from now on. You are not welcome to buy, sell or pass through it.

global.text: Word from {village} is the market is closed until the smoke clears. Wary traders, mind the roads near {player}.
Charcoal and ash both went up this week after {village} burned. Not blaming anyone yet, {player}.
Lost a cart near {village} this morning. Still not sure if {player} saw it or just got lucky.
