Rebuilding {village} will raise the cost of lumber for everyone. Hope the next raid is smaller, honestly.
Keeping my wagons off the east road for now. Nothing personal, {player}, just the usual caution.
Caravans are asking which villages are safe this week. {village} is not on that list anymore.
Anyone buying timber from {village} survivors, come talk to me. I pay fair and fast.
Business as usual in the south. Just watching the roads a little more closely since {village} went up.

whisper.text: {player}, I am not saying it was you. I am saying the timber from {village} has gone up and I am watching the roads.
No hard feelings yet, {player}. Business is business, but I would like to know your plans before I send another wagon out.
Heard the fire in {village} was big. If you want to make it right, sell me a few horses at cost and we can call it even.
I will keep my caravans off roads you are using for now. Let me know if that changes, and I will be happy to talk prices.
Still want to trade, {player}? I can offer a better rate on iron than anyone else in the region. Mind the tolls though.
Tell me honestly, {player}, do you plan on passing through {village} again? It matters for my route planning.
Ash does not sell well, {player}. If you want goods moved out of the region, I can arrange escort for a fee.
I am weighing whether to keep trading with you. Give me a reason to believe this was a one off, and we will see.

global.text: Ser {player} has a name now, and every toll clerk on the road will be happy to spell it wrong on the bill.
Fame does not sell salt. Enjoy the reputation while your carts sit empty, {player}.
Everyone is talking about {player} this week. Shame the talk has not turned into a single fair price.
Funny how a famous face always wants a bigger cut. The tax men will love you, {player}.
Another name rising up the board. I will be watching the ledgers, and I am not impressed yet.
Renown is just debt with better posture. I hope the bill comes due soon, {player}.
{player} is making a name for themselves. Good for them, provided they remember who pays the road wardens.
Heard {player} is suddenly famous. Fame is fine until the caravan guards start asking for a raise.
Quite a reputation building up around {player}. I will keep my prices where they are and see how it goes.
Renown is a curious thing. It brings buyers, it brings thieves, and it brings a great deal of paperwork.
So {player} is on everyone's tongue now. Pass the salt, and let's talk about whether the roads stay open.
Word on the road says {player} has become somebody. I will believe it when the tolls get cheaper.
Did you hear? {player} is the talk of the trade roads now. Rather good for business, I'd say!
Well done, {player}! Your name opens doors faster than any letter of credit I have ever carried.
Our {player} is famous! Half the caravans in Ormerath will want a discount now. Come by the stall, friend.
Fame suits you, {player}. The buyers are chasing you now, so let's make sure the profit follows.
If anyone asks, {player} is a fine partner and a better name to have on a contract. Cheers to that!
Renown looks good on {player}. I expect a few prices to drop in your honour, though I will not be among them.
Lost {fief} to {player}'s banners. The wool market there is about to dry up, and that's on everyone, not just me.
Pour one out for the {fief} merchant guild. They had great margins, and now they have a new landlord who skims everything.
Congrats on {fief}, {player}. Shame the tolls are double now. Caravans will route around it, and you'll have an empty market.
War takes a town and then takes its trade. {fief} will be quiet for months, and I'm not sorry to say I saw it coming.
Anyone hauling salt through {fief} this week, check the gate fees first. I'm not paying them and neither should you.
Heard {player} took {fief}. I'll be sending my caravans around the mountains. Longer road, but at least nobody's shaking me down.

whisper.text: {player}, you took {fief} and now my wagons pay the tax. Enjoy the coin, it's the only thing you'll be getting from me.
Ser {player}, a word of advice. Holding {fief} is expensive. Garrisons eat, and my bread prices aren't going down to help you.
Still haven't forgiven the lost shipment from {fief}, {player}. Remember that when you set your toll rates.
You knew I had a warehouse in {fief}, didn't you? Clever. Clever and rude. Let's not do business for a while.
{player}, I'll keep trading through {fief} if the tolls are fair. Make them fair and we can talk. Otherwise, I'm out.
Congratulations on the capture, {player}. I'll be tallying my losses by candlelight. Expect the invoice to be sent.

global.text: Anyone know what {fief} charges for a stall now? Prices shift every time the banners change. Bad for planning.
{fief} has a new lord. As long as the roads stay open and the tolls stay sane, I'll keep my wagons moving.
Watching the {fief} market settle. Wool's cheaper than last month, so somebody's happy at least.
Caravans are rerouting around {fief} for now. Let's see if the new owners understand what a well-kept road is worth.
Trade doesn't care whose flag is flying. Show me a fair toll and a safe road and I'll show you a busy market.
Quick note for traders: {fief} is open for business again. Bring your goods, bring your coin, and check the price board first.

whisper.text: {player}, I hear you're holding {fief} now. Mind if I send a wagon through? I'll pay the standard toll, no fuss.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Quick question: are the roads patrolled? Bandits are murdering my margins.
Heard the stables in {fief} are still standing. Want to sell any horses there? Fair price, honest weight.
{player}, let's keep things simple. You keep the roads safe, I keep my caravans moving, and everyone eats better.
Would you consider a discount on salt for {fief}'s garrison? Bulk order, prompt payment, and I'll keep my complaints in the ledger.
Still tallying what the siege cost me in {fief}. Not asking for a refund, {player}, just a posted toll schedule.

global.text: Every victory {player} racks up is another road my carts won't be using this week. Lovely for them, not for margins.
Salt is up again. Bet it's the fourth battle this month. Some of us are trying to run a business here.
Half the northern merchants are paying double insurance because of one name on the battle board. Thanks, {player}.
Prices are a mess and it's all because of the fighting. I'd like a refund on my patience, please.
Someone should put a tariff on victories. I'd charge a few gold per win and retire early.
Ten wins in a row and not one of them put a coin in my purse. Wonderful. Truly.
Keep fighting, {player}. Just do it somewhere my caravans aren't scheduled to pass, if you don't mind.

whisper.text: Your little winning streak has my carts stuck at the border for a week. Some of us have deliveries, {player}.
I'm not cheering, I'm counting losses. Three contracts gone since your last battle. Happy now?
You won, and I lost a shipment of dyed cloth. Let's call it even by never meeting again.
Every fight you take makes insurance higher for everyone on the road. Consider that before the next war.
Congratulations on the streak. I'll buy my blades from someone who doesn't cost me a profit from now on.
I'd happily sell you supplies, but after this month I'd rather sell them to anyone else. Nothing personal.
Still angry about the ambush route. I'm not forgiving you until my wagons get paid for.

global.text: Wondering who's buying all the armor lately. Hint: it isn't the farmers.
Keep an eye on the roads, friends. Whoever is winning these fights will want supplies soon.
Nobody asked me, but a winning streak means demand for horses. Stock up before the prices climb.
Fights come and go, but tolls are forever. I'll be watching which roads get busy after this.
Reminder that a victory parade does nothing for the price of salt. Just a thought.
Those battles aren't my business unless someone blocks a road. Until then I'm counting coin, not banners.
Sold four wagonloads of rope today. Whatever is going on out there, it's good for rope.

whisper.text: Heard about your run of wins. Wondering if you'll need horses or just a good price on wagon wheels.
A streak like yours draws attention. Some of it brings buyers. Some of it doesn't. Be careful.
I'm not sure whether to offer you a deal or a warning. Maybe both. Drop by when you have time.
Congratulations, I suppose. Let me know if your next campaign needs supplies and I'll quote you fairly.
Your name keeps coming up at the market. Usually a good sign for me, so I'll keep my ledgers open.
Those roads you've been clearing are useful. If you ever want a steady escort fee, you know where to find me.
Quick question, no pressure: do you plan on buying from anyone, or just winning everything for free?
Winning is one thing. Paying for the wagons afterwards is another. I'd gladly help with the second.

global.text: Two more wins for {player} this week and the whole road is talking. Good for the road, good for my wagons.
If {player} keeps this up, I'll need a bigger warehouse. Bless the chaos, it sells well.
Raising a cup to {player}'s streak. Anyone who needs rope or horses, I'm offering a friend discount.
The banners are up and trade is picking up. Could be the best month my ledger has seen.
Honest question for the market: who else sells to heroes? Because I'm about to get very busy.
Ten wins and the roads are finally safer. Who knew bravery was such a good business model?
Keep the roads clear, {player}. Every cleared road is a new route I can finally afford to use.
Everyone's buying armor this week. I'm happy to be the one selling it, and happier to see you use it well.

whisper.text: Incredible run. I'm putting together a supply list for your next campaign. Want the friend discount?
Seriously, well done. Tell me what your army needs and I'll get it to you at cost. Don't tell the others.
Between your wins and the new road, I might finally retire comfortable. Thank you, truly.
Would you like a retainer? Steady escorts, steady pay, and I'll cover the first month of supplies.
Keep winning and I'll keep my best horses reserved for you. Consider it a standing offer.
Every battle you win means safer carts for my whole network. That's worth a few favours, I think.
Saw your name on the board again. Proud to call you a customer, even if the bill is always large.

global.text: Got released instead of ransomed. Lovely for me, terrible for my ledger. Who's paying for my lost week?
Word to the wise: don't bother taking hostages around here if you won't even collect on them.
Free release, no ransom. Not a business model I'd recommend, {player}.
Lost a fortnight of trade and not one coin of ransom to show for it. Marvelous.
Every caravan I send out now comes with a guard. Thanks for the extra expense, {player}.
Heard {player} let the merchant walk. Pity. A ransom would have financed my next three roads.
Some of us spend our coin on wagons, not sentimental gestures. Dreadful waste of a good hostage.
Freed without a ransom, then wonder why nobody trusts the roads. Hard to fathom, really.

whisper.text: You had me in chains and let me go for nothing? My pride is still bleeding, {player}.
Sending a bill for my wasted week to your door. Don't bother arguing, the number is high.
Next time, ransom me. Two hundred gold would have been fair and we'd both sleep better.
I'll remember this when your caravans hit the road. Not a threat, just a ledger entry.
Freeing me without a ransom makes you look soft, {player}. I doubt that was the plan.
Don't expect a discount on anything from me now. Nothing personal, just bookkeeping.
Released me for free and expect a warm welcome at my stall? Dream on, {player}.
Fine, you let me go. But my prices for you just went up, and I'm not sorry about it.

global.text: Ransom went unpaid, so somebody in Ormerath got a free lesson in economics today.
Freed without a ransom. Odd move. Markets like predictability, and so do I.
Captivity is a poor month for any merchant. Still, I got my boots back, so I'll count it.
Anyone else notice the roads grew quieter after that hostage business? Terrible for margins.
Walked out of captivity with my stock intact. Rare luck. Prices should settle soon, I think.
Didn't pay a penny of ransom and still lost three days. Who's counting the losses today?
Wool is up, salt is up, and I'm finally free. Not sure which of those bothers me more.
Not sure whether to thank {player} or start watching my wallet. Time will tell.

whisper.text: Thanks for the release, {player}. No ransom though, so we're square for now. Just keeping accounts.
Would have preferred a ransom, honestly. Still, I'll note the kindness in my ledger.
Freed me outright? I'm not sure what that costs you. Let me know if you need a horse someday.
No ransom means no debt between us. Fine by me. Consider it an open tab I'll never collect.
I owe you nothing, {player}, which is an unusual feeling for a trader. Ask me about prices sometime.
No ransom, no bill, no grudge. Keep the road clear and we'll call it even.
Your choice to free me without coin is noted. Business is business, though, so mind the tolls.
Had my guards ready to pay, and you just waved me off. Strange trade, {player}, but I'll take it.

global.text: Shoutout to {player} for letting a merchant go without ransom. Good people are good for trade.
Rare sight: a captor who lets the goods walk free. Spread the word, I'll gladly buy a round.
Kind hearts don't usually sell well in this market, but {player} might be the exception.
Free roads, no ransom, no hard feelings. If you're hauling anything, I'll pay for your escort.
Anyone needing a reliable trade partner should know {player} released me with no strings. Recommend.
My purse is light, but my gratitude isn't. Good luck on the road, {player}.
Lost a week, gained a friend. That's a decent exchange rate, if you ask me.
Let's hope the next captive is treated half as fairly. Good for the reputation of all roads here.

whisper.text: You didn't have to let me go for nothing, {player}. I owe you a discount on horses, no argument.
Thank you, truly. First drink of my next shipment is on you whenever you're near the markets.
Released without ransom? I'll give you a fair deal on any wagon, and I don't say that lightly.
Such mercy is bad for my pocket and great for my heart. Expect a warm welcome at my stall.
I hear you're bound for the river roads. Want a guard escort? I'll cover the first leg.
No ransom, no reckoning. If you ever need an inside tip on prices, I'm your ledger.
Say the word and my caravan rides with yours. Free passage, same as you gave me.
Thanks for trusting me to walk away, {player}. I'll make sure my side of the bargain stays honest.

global.text: {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are at war again. My insurance rates just tripled, and nobody asked me first.
Declaring war is easy. Finding a wagon that gets through the mountain passes next month is the hard part.
Whoever started this war, please tell me which roads are still open before you set the bridges on fire.
Wars come and go, but the price of salt never comes back down. Funny how the bills always outlast the banners.
Any toll collector who holds my wagons this week will find I keep very careful records of who owes me.
Selling grain to anyone still hungry after this war. Name your price, I will load the cart by morning.
Bandits love a border war. Half my route is empty now and the other half is full of people with axes.
{enemy_faction} will need tents, sails and rope before this is over. Anyone with spare canvas, now is the time.

whisper.text: Word is {enemy_faction} is squeezing every road out of the east. I can split the cost if you can split the risk.
I don't trust you yet, {player}, but {enemy_faction} is bad for everyone's margins. Shall we talk terms?
Tolls doubled on the river road again. Two traders sharing one escort pay less than two alone. Interested?
No need to like each other. Pool your coin with mine and hire a few swords against {enemy_faction}. Profitable, I promise.
Caravans keep getting hit on the northern pass. Lend me some muscle and I'll cover the wagon fees. Fair?
I'll be blunt, {player}. I want {enemy_faction} off my roads, and you want the same. Let's price it out.
Every week I lose a cart to them, and you probably lose one too. Odd thing for us to agree on, isn't it?
Think of it as a short contract. You keep your trade, I keep my wagons, and {enemy_faction} gets nothing. Deal?
{player}, you're the only honest buyer I've met this season. Let's hit {enemy_faction} together and split the spoils.
Between us, {enemy_faction} owes me eleven wagons. Help me collect and the profit is yours, {player}.
A toast to a fine partnership, {player}! Stand with me against {enemy_faction} and road tolls drop for us both.
Honestly, I'd rather trade with you than fight you. So let's fight {enemy_faction} instead. Tea's on me, friend.
I've been quietly tallying what {enemy_faction} costs us both. The sum is ugly. Shall we make them pay for it?
Good news, {player}: {enemy_faction} is overextended. A joint strike now means cheap iron and fat purses for us.
Ser {player}, a few of your swords beside my wagons would make {enemy_faction} think twice. Are you in?
I don't offer this to just anyone. Ally with me against {enemy_faction} and I'll give you the best rates in the realm.
Word is {enemy_faction} has the road to {fief} shut tight. I need a hand clearing it, and I'll pay fairly for it.
Quick question, {player}: what would a safe escort from {fief} cost me these days? Tolls alone are eating my margin.
{fief} is bleeding coin faster than it bleeds men. If you can spare a few guards, I'll make it worth your while.
I won't pretend I'm not desperate. My carts are stuck behind {enemy_faction} lines and my warehouse is emptying.
Tell me straight, {player}. Is there any profit left in defending {fief}, or should I start selling my wagons now?
Half the grain in {fief} is already spoiling in the rain. Help me move it before the war eats the rest.
Nobody gets rich while the roads burn. Give me a reason to think {fief} is worth backing and we can talk prices.
Hypothetically, what would you charge to put a company of swords on the {fief} road? Strictly business, mind.
We've done good business together, {player}, so I'll be blunt. {fief} is under pressure and I could use your sword arm.
Remember that spice deal? Let's make a new one. I'm offering a generous cut if you help keep {fief} standing.
Friend, my caravans are idle and my coffers are thinner than a bandit's excuse. Can you spare some hands for {fief}?
If {enemy_faction} takes {fief}, every road I trade on turns into a toll gate. Help me hold it and the discount is yours.
I trust you more than most, which is why I'm asking first. Ride with me to {fief} and I'll cover your supplies.
Honest truth, I'm not sure how long {fief} can hold. Could you lend a blade or two? I'll owe you a favor.
Between us, I've already lost two wagons this month. Help me keep {fief} open and I'll throw in a fine horse.
You've never let me down on a fair deal, so I'll ask plainly: will you help save {fief} from {enemy_faction}?
Your last stunt cost me three wagons of salt, {player}. Meet me on the road outside {town} and we settle it with steel.
Every contract you touch goes sour, {player}. I'm done haggling. Name a field and bring your best sword.
Think your guards can keep my caravan safe? Prove it. Dawn at the crossroads near {village}, one on one.
I've priced out every option, and the cheapest way to end this is a duel. Meet me at the {town} gates, {player}.
A fight would cost us both gold, but I'd rather watch you lose yours. Come to {village} at noon.
Stop hiding behind your hired blades, {player}. Face me yourself in the open field past {town}.
I'll drop the trade talk. You cut my margins, so I'll cut your purse back, in person. Pick the ground.
Lost my goods to your men twice now. Third time I'd rather settle the account in a proper challenge. {village} bridge, sundown.
Nothing personal, {player}, but my toll roads need defending and you're in the way. Shall we test it? Fair terms, one bout.
Heard you're a capable blade. I'd rather know that than guess. Meet me near {town} for a friendly bout, winner keeps the bet.
Proposal: a short duel at {village} for a purse of ten silver. Win or lose, we both walk away owing nothing.
Sizing up the competition, {player}. A bout outside {town} would settle who controls the eastern road. Interested?
No grudge here, just a wager. Ride out to {village} and let's see whose coin holds up under steel.
The valley trade is getting crowded. Care to settle the matter with a duel instead of a price war, {player}?
Before we both lose money undercutting each other, why not fight it out once? Meet me at {town} crossroads, swords only.
Odds are fifty-fifty and I dislike leaving things unsettled. A challenge at {village}, {player}, if you're willing.
Still walking everywhere, {player}? Shame. Coin never fattens a cart that stays on foot.
I checked the market board. Your wares are priced like yesterday's bread. Hard to watch, honestly.
Every trader I know keeps a spare wagon. You have a pack mule and a prayer. Bold strategy.
Tell me, {player}, do you count your coins before or after the bandits take them?
I'd offer you a loan, but I've read your ledger. Dreadful reading. Keep your chin up.
Walked past your stall twice today. Nobody stopped. Not even the pigeons. Strange how that works.
Your last caravan earned less than it paid in tolls. I did the sums. Rather sad, really.
Honest advice: stop bidding against {rival}'s buyers. They already know exactly what you'll accept.
